about:
Charles River Apparel is based in Sharon, Massachusetts. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed in the available sources.

The company offers a range of branded apparel for men, women, and unisex categories, including quarter-zip pullovers, sweatshirts, jackets, and parkas. Proprietary fabric technologies such as TexturKnit™ and Flex-Fleece™ are featured across the product line. One listed fabric composition consists of 59% cotton, 38% recycled polyester, and 3% spandex in a textured knit weighing 8.70 oz/yd². The company also provides decoration services for its garments.

The brand serves the consumer apparel market directly through its website, offering styles such as the Willow Mock-Neck Sweatshirt, Cayak Lightweight Stretch Quarter Zip Pullover, Coastal Sweatshirt, Lotus Hybrid Puffer Jacket, Heathered Fleece Jacket, and Odyssey Waterproof Parka. No specific industrial or institutional customer segments are identified in the available information.

No stated mission or founding purpose is provided in the source material.

name: Charleston Woodworking School
old_description: .  Founded by Master Craftsman Sam Sprouse, the school offer students a professional learning environment. Sam is a graduate of the prestigious Thomas Chippendale School of Furniture in Scotland.
about:
Located in Charleston, South Carolina, the Charleston Woodworking School was founded by Master Craftsman Sam Sprouse, a graduate of the Thomas Chippendale School of Furniture in Scotland. The school operates from a state-of-the-art facility and is licensed by the South Carolina Commission on Higher Education.

The school delivers a nine-month professional woodworking program that emphasizes traditional techniques. Curriculum covers furniture design, furniture making, antique restoration and repair, specialty wood projects, project management, and marketing. Instruction combines classroom theory with hands-on shop work; each student designs and builds a major furniture piece per semester. Enrollment is capped at 15 students per academic year to ensure one-on-one tutoring and a self-paced learning environment. The shop remains open after hours for independent project development.

The program serves individuals seeking a career in woodworking, including veterans who can use VA benefits. Graduates are prepared to pursue furniture design, custom furniture making, antique restoration, or to launch their own woodworking businesses. The school also teaches marketing strategies aimed at interior designers, home builders, antique dealers, and private clients.

Differentiators cited by the school include its status as the only professional woodworking school in South Carolina, VA-approved benefits, small class sizes, a faculty of local woodworking experts and business professionals, and a sustainability focus that prioritizes locally harvested lumber.

name: Charter Wire
old_description: A Leading Cold Rolled and Formed Steel Manufacturer Since 1936
about:
Charter Wire was founded in 1936 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The company operates as a member of the privately held Charter Manufacturing family of companies, which provides vertical integration across steel production, casting, and recycling through sister operations Charter Steel, Charter Casting, and Niles Iron and Metal Company.

The company specializes in cold rolling and forming, producing engineered shaped wire, cold finished bar, and cold-headed and stamped components. It operates two facilities in Milwaukee, serving as a tier 1 supplier for these product lines, with capabilities in cold heading and stamping alongside its core rolling and forming processes.

Charter Wire serves the automotive, agriculture, construction, consumer, industrial, and oil and gas sectors, supplying components that meet the demands of each industry. Its customer base includes tier 1 automotive suppliers and original equipment manufacturers across these markets.

Its core values—trust, teamwork, safety, and continuous improvement—have guided the business across four generations and underpin its approach to customer relationships.

name: Chicago Protective Apparel Inc
old_description: PUT US TO THE TEST WITH FACILITY ASSESSMENTS TO IMPROVE WORK SAFETY AND PRODUCTION
about:
Chicago Protective Apparel Inc operates from Skokie, Illinois, where it maintains its headquarters The company does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or the names of its founders.

The firm produces a range of protective apparel organized into specialized catalogs for arc flash, foundry, and welding applications. Its product lines include aluminized PPE for high-heat environments, flame-resistant clothing, cut- and mechanical-resistant garments, chemical protective apparel, and everyday workwear. The company also publishes a face shield catalog and a fire catalog, suggesting a breadth of protective equipment beyond garments. In addition to selling finished products, Chicago Protective Apparel offers on-site facility assessments aimed at improving workplace safety and production efficiency.

Customers span industries where thermal, electrical, and chemical hazards are present, including welding operations, metal foundries, electrical utilities and contractors, chemical processing plants, and general manufacturing facilities requiring daily protective wear. The company's website serves multiple regions, with language options for North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific markets.

The company positions its facility assessment service as a key differentiator, inviting prospective clients to test its expertise in identifying safety gaps and recommending appropriate protective solutions. Its catalogs, such as the CPA 2112 Catalog, reference specific industry standards, though the company does not list certifications on its public profile.

name: Chisel & Wood
old_description: With the use of solid american hardwoods, we get the privilege of telling the story of that wood and bringing it back to life through the means of making custom furniture.
about:
Chisel & Wood operates from a studio woodshop on an 11-acre property in Dadeville, Alabama. The business was founded in 2019 by Zach, a woodworker raised in Northern Michigan and trained in Northern California. After leaving his previous job, he drove cross-country to California where Chisel & Wood began in a friend's workshop with minimal equipment. He then attended the Krenov School of Fine Woodworking in Fort Bragg before returning to Alabama to build his current shop.

The company designs and builds custom furniture using solid American hardwoods. All work — design, lumber selection, milling, machining, joinery, sanding, and finishing — is performed in-house in a climate-controlled, 1,500-square-foot workshop. The space is organized into functional tool islands and centers around a traditional workbench where handplanes and other hand tools are used for detailed work.

Chisel & Wood serves residential customers seeking handcrafted furniture for the home. Its pieces are marketed directly to homeowners through the company's website and portfolio.

The founder's training at the Krenov School and emphasis on hand-tool craftsmanship distinguish the operation. Zach has stated that the business exists to tell the story of each piece of wood and to maintain excellence by controlling every step of the process.

name: Choice Electronics
old_description: refurbished Sencore models, for use in all areas of the service
about:
Choice Electronics is based in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Founded in 1994 by Lance and Christin Tople, the company began as a provider of refurbished test equipment for the service industry.

The company specializes in refurbishing used test equipment to a like-new condition, focusing on Sencore models but also handling Tektronix and Hewlett Packard units. It operates a refurbishment process that restores equipment to near-new performance, backed by a six-month warranty. Choice Electronics also offers NIST-traceable calibration standards on most refurbished units and provides repair and calibration services for equipment not originally purchased from them. The company stocks new Sencore LC103 units with a one-year warranty and distributes new B&K products at discounted prices.

Choice Electronics serves the service industry, including technicians and professionals who rely on test equipment for maintenance and repair work. Its customer base spans more than 30 countries, indicating an international reach. The company caters to buyers seeking cost-effective alternatives to new test equipment, offering savings up to 80 percent off new prices.

The company emphasizes the quality of its refurbishment process, claiming that its refurbished Sencore equipment is in better condition than any other used units on the market. It was started to provide professionals with reliable, affordable test equipment without the need to buy new.

about:
Chris Haynes Electric Supply Inc. operates from Jackson, Mississippi, where it was founded in 1963 by Chris P. Haynes Sr. The family-owned business has remained under Haynes family leadership, with Chris P. Haynes Jr. serving as president for the past three decades. The company began as a local electrical supply house serving the Jackson area and has grown into a major regional distributor.

The company maintains a 28,500-square-foot warehouse on South West Street, which it describes as the largest single-location stock of electrical supplies in Mississippi. From this facility, the firm stocks and distributes a broad range of electrical products. Its fleet of trucks delivers materials throughout most of the state, and the company also ships orders nationwide.

Chris Haynes Electric Supply serves contractors, maintenance departments, and other buyers in the Jackson metropolitan area and across Mississippi. The company emphasizes its experienced staff and their product knowledge as key to helping customers identify and obtain the correct parts quickly.

The business was built on a commitment to order accuracy and timely delivery. Management states that its strength lies in getting the right parts to the customer when they are needed and prides itself on getting orders right the first time.

name: Circa Energy
old_description: Produce your own electricity by going solar with Circa Energy.
about:
Based in Annapolis, Maryland, Circa Energy is a family-owned solar installation company led by owner Chip and chief operating officer Elena. The firm has been serving the region since at least 2019, focusing on residential photovoltaic projects and offering a turnkey experience that covers every regulatory step.

The company provides full-service solar installation, handling permit acquisition, inspection coordination, and the physical installation of panels and microinverters. All project phases are managed in-house, from initial design through final commissioning, with no subcontracting of core installation work.

Circa Energy primarily serves homeowners in the Annapolis area seeking to reduce electricity costs and gain energy predictability. Customer reviews highlight complex roof configurations, emergency repair work after storm damage, and projects requiring coordination with utility rebate deadlines as examples of projects the team has completed.

The company emphasizes a personal, transparent approach, with the owners directly involved in customer communication and problem resolution. Clients cite the firm's willingness to address warranty issues beyond contractual obligations, its ability to meet aggressive timelines, and the continuity of having the same points of contact throughout the project lifecycle as key differentiators.

name: City Bench
old_description: Each year millions of these grand, historic trees come down across the country due to weather, development, and disease.
about:
City Bench operates from a shop in Higganum, Connecticut, with a milling facility in nearby Hamden. The company was founded by Ted Esselstyn and Zeb Esselstyn as a limited liability company. The idea emerged when Ted, an artist and furniture maker, was working on a Connecticut Trash Museum exhibit about throw-away culture and recognized that street trees removed by municipalities could be upcycled into meaningful furniture.

The company transforms urban trees—salvaged from cities, towns, and institutions—into one-of-a-kind furniture, slabs, and lumber. Workflows include design, milling, fabrication, and final assembly, all performed by hand at their Connecticut shops. The team includes shop manager Ben Komola and sculptor Mike Donovan, though total headcount is not disclosed.

City Bench serves education and nonprofit clients such as Yale University, Harvard University, and the University of Connecticut; commercial customers including PepsiCo, Bridgewater Associates, and lululemon; museums like the Florence Griswold Museum and Mystic Seaport Museum; and healthcare institutions such as Yale New Haven Hospital and Connecticut Children’s Medical Center. The company also works directly with municipalities, arborists, architects, and interior designers.

Each piece ships with a “birth certificate” documenting the tree’s origin and story, reflecting the founders’ goal to create positive environmental and social change by turning a waste stream into a value stream.

name: City Food Equipment - Lombard, IL - New & Used Restaurant Equipment & Kitchen Supply Store
old_description: City Food Equipment - Lombard, IL - New and Used Restaurant Equipment & Kitchen Supply Store
about:
City Food Equipment operates a 45,000-square-foot store and showroom in Lombard, Illinois, a village in DuPage County about 22 miles west of Chicago. The facility is open to the public six days a week, offering wholesale pricing to both food-service professionals and home cooks.

The company stocks new and used commercial restaurant equipment from brands such as Hobart, Vulcan, True Manufacturing, and Manitowoc, with up to 1,000 pieces on display at any time. An in-house team of technicians inspects, repairs, and refurbishes each used unit before it reaches the sales floor, a process the company says covers meat-processing, deli, and bakery machinery. The showroom also carries thousands of smallwares and supplies for front- and back-of-house needs.

Customers include restaurants, bars, bakeries, delis, catering operations, and meat-processing facilities, as well as individual home chefs. The product range spans cooking equipment (ranges, fryers, ovens, griddles, charbroilers), refrigeration, meat-processing tools (grinders, slicers, saws, mixers, stuffers), and bakery mixers and dividers.

City Food Equipment describes itself as one of the nation's largest used-restaurant-equipment dealers and highlights its certified technicians who refurbish Hobart planetary mixers to original manufacturer specifications. The company emphasizes its rigorous restoration process and the breadth of inventory available for immediate purchase.
